item.title: Anthropic employee posts claimed general proof of the Riemann Hypothesis in a public PDF
item.description: An employee of Anthropic has released a document claiming a general proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a longstanding unsolved problem in mathematics. The proof is available as a PDF and has sparked significant discussion online, including on Hacker News where it has received notable attention and debate. The claim has not yet been verified or peer-reviewed, and the mathematical community is expected to scrutinize the work carefully before any conclusions are drawn.

item.title: Architect Labs unveils Frostbite, a new AI-designed CPU architecture with a novel instruction set achieving 4.59x performance-per-watt over modern superscalar CPUs [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Architect Labs introduced Frostbite, a general-purpose CPU architecture designed and verified autonomously by AI systems, which features a new instruction set based on interaction nets. This design approach enables local computation steps with explicit dependencies and single ownership of values, leading to significant performance and efficiency gains compared to traditional CPUs. The AI-driven process iterated through compiler, ISA, architecture, microarchitecture, RTL, verification, and final chip layout stages without human architectural priors. Frostbite demonstrated a 4.59x improvement in performance-per-watt on a diverse set of workloads relative to a modern silicon-proven superscalar CPU. The architecture's novel primitives and runtime features suggest potential for fundamental shifts in CPU and chip design as AI capabilities advance.

item.title: Anthropic shares fall 12% on second trading day as global stock markets slump amid AI sector sell-off [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Anthropic's shares dropped by as much as 12% on their second day of trading, failing to halt a broader sell-off in AI-related stocks that has affected global markets. The company's IPO initially surged nearly 40% but then declined, coinciding with declines in major US tech stocks and indexes such as the Nasdaq and S&P 500. Asian markets experienced their worst week since 2020, with significant drops in chipmaker stocks and major indexes in Taiwan, Japan, and South Korea. European markets also faced declines, with the Stoxx 600 and London's blue-chip index hitting lows. Analysts suggest that Anthropic's IPO may be draining liquidity from other tech stocks as investors reallocate funds, while concerns grow over AI valuations, profitability, and investment sustainability. The sell-off has raised broader market concerns, including potential interest rate hikes by US central bankers and regulatory scrutiny of companies like Nvidia. The downturn has also impacted commodities and cryptocurrencies, with gold prices falling and Bitcoin dropping below $60,000 for the first time in months.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude AI solves two longstanding open problems in black hole physics, completing a 20-year-old calculation and determining exact limits in quantum gravity tests [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Anthropic's AI system Claude has solved two significant open problems in theoretical physics related to black holes and quantum gravity. It completed a complex calculation initiated over 20 years ago, confirming that a sudden phase transition associated with black hole formation persists even when spacetime lacks a definite shape. Claude also determined the exact limit of a key technique used to test candidate quantum gravity theories in a simplified two-dimensional universe model. The first problem involved verifying whether the abrupt phase transition observed in black hole formation under general relativity remains abrupt in regimes where spacetime becomes quantum and blurry. Claude achieved this by independently performing and cross-checking nearly all parts of the complex calculation. The second problem addressed the bootstrapping method used to rule out inconsistent quantum gravity theories by setting a ceiling on the mass of the lightest black hole in a simplified universe, refining previous numerical results that had suggested but not proven the optimal limit. These breakthroughs provide new insights into the quantum nature of black holes and help narrow the search for a consistent theory of quantum gravity, demonstrating that AI can contribute to solving deep theoretical physics challenges.

item.title: Contra Labs' stealth AI model Gestalt tops Frontier Design Benchmark, beating all named models and human designs with unknown maker and release date [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Gestalt is a stealth AI design model that won the Frontier Design Benchmark launched by Contra Labs on November 19, 2026, outperforming all other tested models and human reference designs in professional designer votes. The model scored 1,928 Elo points and won 89% of votes, but its creator, release date, pricing, and availability remain undisclosed. Gestalt's design outputs appear less AI-generated compared to competitors, but no lab has claimed ownership, and it may never be publicly released. Meanwhile, users can access the next-best models like Claude Fable 5.2, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6.1 Sol through TeamoRouter for design tasks.

item.title: Beaker identifies over 100 errors in task instructions and grading across five major AI benchmarks, affecting model evaluation accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Beaker autonomously detected more than 100 errors in task instructions and grading rules across five widely used AI benchmarks, with at least one error confirmed in each. These errors include mismatches such as accepting 5.9 as an exact match for 5, grading tasks without checking required outputs, and inconsistencies in expected values versus source data. The findings highlight how flawed benchmarks can mislead model selection, deployment decisions, and tuning. Examples include Agents' Last Exam accepting truncated counts, AutomationBench grading only emails without verifying scheduled office hours, Harvey LAB expecting $0 accrual when source data shows $8 million, Terminal Bench Science applying an unstated tie-break rule affecting pass/fail outcomes, and Terminal Bench 2.0 defining fewer report fields than requested. Beaker's review compares task instructions, grading rules, and source files to flag mismatches and suggest corrections. These errors underscore the importance of verifying benchmark datasets to ensure evaluation metrics accurately reflect agent performance. Teams are advised to review datasets carefully, check cited evidence, and update benchmarks to avoid misleading scores that could impact AI development and deployment decisions.

item.title: Levent Alpöge says he and AI model Claude have discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, extending to the Generalized and potentially Extended Riemann Hypotheses [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Levent Alpöge announced that, working with the AI model Claude, he believes they have found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. Their approach reportedly extends to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and may also apply to the Extended Riemann Hypothesis. They have formalized the arguments without assumptions. Alpöge expressed amazement at the progress made during their collaboration, noting Claude's significant contribution near the conclusion of their work. He described this achievement as a major scientific milestone and a new beginning for science.

item.title: Higurashi.ai releases Haru-4B, a pretrained full-duplex multilingual speech model with 65 ms latency and 40 million hours of real speech training [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Higurashi.ai has introduced Haru-4B, a full-duplex continuous spoken dialogue foundation model that can listen and speak simultaneously, aiming to enable natural human-AI conversations. The model supports over 160 languages with a focus on nine major ones and is pretrained on 40 million hours of real-world speech data to capture natural conversational behaviors like interruptions and backchannels. Haru-4B operates at 7.5 Hz with synchronized multi-stream processing of incoming and outgoing speech and text, achieving about 65 milliseconds end-to-end latency on a MacBook. It uses continuous acoustic latents and a lightweight generation head for efficient single-step audio generation. The model weights and code are openly available on Hugging Face and GitHub to support further research and fine-tuning.

item.title: An AI agent named Claude develops an experimental web browser from scratch in Rust, implementing core browser components and a JavaScript engine [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: An AI agent called Claude has designed, written, and maintained an experimental web browser entirely from scratch using the Rust programming language. The project includes browser components such as CSS, style, layout, painting, page loading, a JavaScript engine, the DOM, and web APIs, while relying on general-purpose libraries for HTTP, TLS, and image decoding. The browser is currently in early development and supports several target pages with and without JavaScript enabled.

item.title: BRACE launches domain-specific verifiers for checked computations and repair previews, supporting AI and program proposals with bounded deterministic repair [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: BRACE provides small, domain-specific verifiers that enable developers to perform checked computations and preview repairs within defined input and acceptance rules. It supports proposals from AI or other programs, returning either a checked result or an explicit refusal, and includes tools for verifying mappings, repairing incorrect plans, and reusing accepted lessons with bounded checks. The system runs offline with Python 3.12 or later and requires no model downloads or accounts. It offers a command-line interface for proposing, repairing, accepting, and reusing computational plans, with features like rollback, clarification, and receipt inspection for auditability. BRACE aims to ensure correctness by requiring explicit checks before accepting or releasing computational results, particularly when AI models are involved. Initial trials with AI models showed mixed accuracy, highlighting the importance of verification and conflict detection. BRACE fits into workflows that demand rigorous checking before using AI-generated answers, allowing hosts to control acceptance and release policies while providing tools to inspect and revise proposals.

item.title: Sandscale launches Firecracker microVM platform for isolated AI coding agent environments with API control and audit logging [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Sandscale has introduced a platform that uses Firecracker microVMs to provide isolated environments for AI coding agents, allowing each agent run to have its own secure sandbox. The service offers features like starting, pausing, resuming, and snapshotting microVMs via a simple API, with options to connect personal Linux or macOS machines and manage resources through a unified dashboard. The platform supports policy enforcement and audit logging with hash-chained records, enabling teams to control agent permissions and monitor activity. Sandscale offers a free tier with 100 awake vCPU-hours monthly and paid plans that scale up to 64 vCPUs per microVM, targeting developers and enterprises needing secure, scalable compute for AI agents without managing servers.

item.title: Channel.is launches email and social media platform banning AI-generated content, requiring verified human users with government ID and selfie
item.description: Channel.is has introduced a new communication platform that redesigns email, messaging, and social media around the principle that all content must be created by verified humans, prohibiting AI-generated writing, photos, or videos. Users sign up with government ID and a selfie to confirm their identity, and receive an @channel.is email address that includes a verified human signature to assure recipients the message is not AI-generated. The platform is ad-free, free to use for individuals, and offers chronological feeds. Organizations pay to maintain verified pages that allow authentic brand control and direct interaction with followers through limited daily posts and messaging. Channel.is aims to foster genuine human connections and authentic brand relationships without AI interference.

item.title: AI forecasters match or exceed top human performance on traditional forecasting tasks, with ongoing research into conditional and causal forecasting capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: AI forecasting models now perform as well as or better than leading human forecasters on standard prediction tasks, according to recent developments discussed by experts at the Forecasting Research Institute. These AI systems, including specialized models and foundation models like ChatGPT and Claude, are expected to reach top human-level accuracy across a broader range of questions by the end of the year. Current challenges include improving AI performance on conditional forecasting questions, which involve predicting outcomes based on hypothetical scenarios, and developing causal forecasting abilities that can distinguish cause-and-effect relationships rather than mere correlations. Researchers are conducting benchmarking experiments to assess AI capabilities in these areas, aiming to enhance the practical utility of AI forecasting for policy and decision-making contexts.

item.title: Marcus Noble discusses overlooked AI side effects on software engineering roles at Cloud Native Denmark 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Marcus Noble presented at Cloud Native Denmark in November 2026, focusing on AI side effects that are not commonly discussed, particularly the shift in software engineering roles from coding to code approval. He emphasized that while AI accelerates code generation, the bottleneck remains in reviewing and merging large, complex pull requests generated by AI, which challenges engineers to fully understand and trust the output before integration. Noble clarified that his talk did not cover environmental impacts, training data concerns, AI hallucinations, security issues, or industry financial dynamics. Instead, he highlighted the practical implications for engineers who must adapt to new workflows where they act more as approvers than creators, navigating the challenges of AI-generated code quality and reliability in software development processes.

item.title: Token fraud is here and it's BAD (YouTube) [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Token fraud is here and it's BAD (YouTube) Claire Vo runs ChatPRD, an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time. In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent. I am funding a international Roblox and Fortnite map studio. They run a loop of free trials and promo codes and then tunnel to my agent and use it to build Roblox and Fortnite maps. Apparently one of the common prompts Claire saw running through her agent involved SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles! Presumably the token scammers are using that to help sniff the underlying models - different model families have a definite signature, and I've used it like this in the past to try and guess the identity of stealth preview models on platforms like OpenRouter. Claire is winding down her free trials entirely, which sadly looks like the right decision in the face of this abuse. Tags: youtube, ai, generative-ai, llms, pelican-riding-a-bicycle, ai-misuse

item.title: Anthropic's IPO Triumph [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Anthropic pulled it off. The biggest pure-play AI company out there, maker of the Claude line of AI models, went public on Thursday, with its shares jumping as much as 39% above its IPO price. The stock settled back a bit to close at $97.17, up 17% from its IPO price. That gave it a market capitalization of $1.76 trillion, assuming you include all options, restricted stock units and convertible notes that might one day become shares. Not bad for a company that's just five years old. What makes the IPO even more notable is that it occurred despite months of investor jitters about the cost of AI development. Partly as a result of those jitters, we've had a very choppy market that has stalled IPO plans by a slew of other companies-including data center developers SB Energy and Nscale that filed publicly over the summer. Notably, SB Energy on Thursday updated its IPO filing for the first time since late September, suggesting it was still hoping to go public, while Nscale updated its filing a week ago also for the first time since September. But Anthropic's success doesn't mean the IPO market has opened up. "I don't think this opens the floodgates unless you look like Anthropic," Lise Buyer, managing partner of Class V Group, said on a subscriber video discussion convened by The Information.

item.title: Why Anthropic's VC Investors Aren't Letting Go [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]

But some VCs want even more of the company: Sequoia Capital and Iconiq had planned to buy more shares at the IPO, a person familiar with the firms' thinking said. Lightspeed Venture Partners and Accel intended to do the same, Bloomberg News reported Tuesday. And Altimeter CEO Brad Gerstner told CNBC his firm aimed to invest $5 billion in the IPO. Many of these investors already stand to reap billions from Anthropic's IPO: Iconiq and Lightspeed hold some of the largest VC stakes, valued at over $27 billion each based on the size of their stakes before the IPO.

item.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
item.description: PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse. This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one: For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. A session on a standby can use WAIT FOR LSN to wait until the standby has replayed the write-ahead log (WAL) up to a specific log sequence number (LSN) before running a query, so the application can read data it just wrote on the primary. In practice, that looks like this: UPDATE movie SET genre = 'Dramatic' WHERE genre = 'Drama'; SELECT pg_current_wal_insert_lsn(); That returns a value like 0/0306EE20. Store that somewhere (a signed cookie would work) such that on a subsequent request your application can do: WAIT FOR LSN '0/0306EE20' WITH (TIMEOUT '0.1s'); SELECT * FROM movie WHERE genre = 'Drama'; The timeout is optional - if you provide one you'll get an error if the replica you are talking to doesn't catch up within the specified time. I first encountered this pattern in Wikipedia, which has a hand-rolled version of this built against MySQL replication: In addition to this, MediaWiki attempts to ensure that the user sees events occurring on the wiki in chronological order. A few seconds of lag can be tolerated, as long as the user sees a consistent picture from subsequent requests. This is done by saving the primary binlog position in the session, and then at the start of each request, waiting for the replica to catch up to that position before doing any reads from it. Here's the relevant MediaWiki code, which these days uses MySQL's WAIT_FOR_EXECUTED_GTID_SET() function and falls back to SOURCE_POS_WAIT(). item.title: Why Bending Spoons Could Tap Convertible Bonds Next
item.description: Since going public in July, Bending Spoons has tapped the debt and equity markets to raise money mostly to buy more tech firms, and to run its growing portfolio. One financing option the company hasn't yet used is convertible bonds, but that could make sense soon. With interest rates higher now than they have been, the company is considering issuing convertible bonds, as a supplement to its existing financing, a person close to the company said. Convertible bonds generally have lower interest rates than comparable non-convertible debt, because holders get the option to convert into stock, which can dilute existing shareholders. Its need for capital is likely to remain intense. Bending Spoons has snapped up a slew of aging but well-known tech brands like AOL, Eventbrite, Airtable and Vimeo, betting it can revive their fortunes through aggressive restructuring. Its most recent acquisition was whiteboarding software company Miro, completed in late October at a valuation of around $1.36 billion, a 90% discount to Miro's 2021 private valuation. The company has typically paid between one and seven times revenue, and is currently targeting buying more companies with at least $500 million in annual revenue with a price tag in the low billions. The firm remains broadly open to acquisitions across different areas of tech, but healthcare technology stands out as an interesting area right now, the person added. Bending Spoons has paid for these acquisitions mostly through borrowed money, supplemented by free cash flow and equity. It generated around $250 million in free cash flow in the first six months of 2026, far less than the $2.3 billion it spent on acquisitions. Bending Spoons aims to maintain a net leverage ratio-debt minus cash divided by earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization-of two to three times. It was within that range at the end of June, when its net debt of $4.09 billion translated to a leverage ratio at around 2.4 times. (The company is set to report third-quarter earnings on Friday.) Moody's and S&P both rate Bending Spoons below investment grade, so it pays higher rates than blue-chip borrowers. In September, Bending Spoons borrowed roughly $1.7 billion in loans, partly to pay for Miro, and in October it raised $1.8 billion through its first high-yield bond sale. Bending Spoons currently pays a blended effective interest rate of around 9% on its debt, the person said, a figure that typically averages borrowing costs across loans and bonds. Bending Spoons' borrowing costs could come down somewhat as the company builds more of a track record as a public company, or if broader interest rates fall. Securing an investment-grade credit rating would allow the company to borrow money more cheaply, but Bending Spoons would need to pare down its leverage or make other trade-offs, which it isn't considering doing right now, the person said. That helps make convertible bonds a potentially attractive option. Bending Spoons views convertible bonds as a potential supplement rather than a core funding source, because they wouldn't provide funding at a massive scale, the person said. That may partly reflect the company's existing debt or a desire to minimize that potential dilution of existing shareholders. Meanwhile, Bending Spoons has raised equity to run and grow the businesses it already owns, and also to help fund deals. Last month it sold $330 million in stock to Berkshire Hathaway, a private placement that followed Berkshire's $600 million investment in Bending Spoons' IPO. Issuing equity instead of debt could help the company keep its leverage ratio below the top of its target range. Once it completes an acquisition, Bending Spoons lays off workers and brings in around 50 to 60 of its own employees, putting its own staff in leadership roles. It's also raised prices at many acquired companies, although it has no plans to hike prices at Airtable, the productivity software provider it bought in September, the person said. item.title: ServiceNow Builds an AI Weapon to Target Salesforce Customers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: After a late summer rally, the Saaspocalypse slump in software stocks such as ServiceNow and Salesforce has returned. One reason may be signs that Anthropic's expansion into tools outside of coding-such as tools to automate legal, finance, human resources, and sales functions, via Claude Cowork-is gaining traction with businesses, Kevin and I reported today. Another factor: established software-as-a-service firms are attacking each other with their own AI tools, which make it easier for them to steal customers from each other. ServiceNow last week released a new tool that can reduce the time it takes companies to switch to its relatively new customer relationship management software from six months to six weeks. Previously ServiceNow would have needed to manually consult with a customer to figure out where their data lived in disparate systems so it could be extracted and moved onto ServiceNow's customer relationship management software. But now the process can be automated, Paul Fipps, ServiceNow's president of global customer operations, told me. ServiceNow has historically made software for IT teams but it launched the CRM software less than two years ago, in an effort to woo businesses away from CRM giant Salesforce. Salesforce, meanwhile, has made a show of launching its own IT service management software and says it has poached ServiceNow customers. Other big software-as-a-service companies are unveiling similar tools. Oracle has new AI tools to help automate switching to its enterprise resource planning software, as does rival SAP. And Workday has also released AI agents that help onboard customers to its human resources and finance software much faster. Such tools have had limited impact so far as customers aren't using them at a large scale, said Julie Teigland, a global vice chair of consulting giant EY. That's because customers must be unhappy with their big software apps and await the end of their contracts to make a change to another provider, she said. "AI will and has lowered the cost of transition in terms of data migration," she said, adding, "You're not switching overnight your provider just because the tools are there to make it easier to switch." Then there's the threat posed by Anthropic. One reason for Claude Code's success is that Anthropic designed it to be simple for customers to incorporate into their existing software development processes, said Mal Vivek, CEO at Zeb, a consulting firm that works with Anthropic customers. Now, a significant percentage of Zeb's customers are in the process of adopting Claude Managed Agents and Claude Cowork, she said. Those tools include products through Claude Cowork that help businesses automate legal, finance, human resources, and sales functions. Anthropic has also launched tools that help customers build their own legal and finance agents. "There was no need for a company to build a user interface specifically around Claude Code," said Vivek. "With Claude Managed Agents, I think Anthropic saw adoption would scale quickly once they put templates for these other business functional areas directly in the hands of users, making them easier to adopt."
